_note: Rhode Island fee rules, retrieved verbatim from the R.I. Legislature statute server (webserver.rilegislature.gov) on 2026-06-20. Sources (Title 34 Ch. 18): § 34-18-59 (Fair limitation on rental application fees — a landlord may not require a prospective tenant to pay a rental application fee; background/credit checks are limited to actual cost and only when the tenant has not supplied a recent one); § 34-18-61 (Convenience fees prohibited — no convenience fee may be charged on a rent payment, unless a no-fee payment method is also accepted); § 34-18-15(a)(1) (fees beyond rent must be disclosed in the lease in the same section as the rent disclosure). IMPORTANT: Rhode Island has NO statutory cap or prohibition on late fees (confirmed against the Ch. 18 index — there is no late-fee section), so NO late-fee 'illegal' rule is written here; doing so would invent law. ALL rules status=draft-unverified: must be reviewed by a Rhode Island tenant attorney / legal-aid clinic before public conclusions.

rules.title: Rental application fee charged to a prospective tenant
rules.description: Per R.I. Gen. Laws § 34-18-59(a), a landlord, lessor, sub-lessor, real estate broker, property management company, or designee may not require or demand that a prospective tenant pay a rental application fee. (A background or credit check may be charged at no more than actual cost, and only when the applicant has not supplied a recent one — § 34-18-59(b).) A flat 'application fee' or 'processing fee' charged to apply is prohibited.
rules.tenant_explainer: In Rhode Island a landlord can't charge you a fee just to apply for an apartment. They can pass on the actual cost of a background or credit check (and only if you didn't already give them a recent one) — but a flat application or processing fee isn't allowed.

citations.label: R.I. Gen. Laws § 34-18-59(a)
citations.quote: A landlord, lessor, sub-lessor, real estate broker, property management company, or designee shall not be allowed to require or demand any prospective tenant to pay for a rental application fee.

rules.title: Convenience fee added to a rent payment
rules.description: Per R.I. Gen. Laws § 34-18-61(a), a landlord may not charge a convenience fee on a tenant's rent payment. The only exception (§ 34-18-61(b)) is when the landlord also accepts a payment method that carries no such fee. A clause adding a surcharge, 'convenience fee', or processing fee to online/card rent payments without a free alternative is prohibited.
rules.tenant_explainer: Your landlord can't tack a 'convenience fee' onto your rent — for example a surcharge for paying online or by card — unless they also give you a way to pay that has no fee.

citations.label: R.I. Gen. Laws § 34-18-61(a)
citations.quote: A landlord shall not charge a convenience fee to a tenant’s rental payment.

rules.title: Undisclosed fees beyond rent
rules.description: Per R.I. Gen. Laws § 34-18-15(a)(1), if fees beyond the rent apply to the unit, the lease must disclose them in the same section as the rent disclosure and indicate that additional fees may apply. A clause reserving the landlord's right to impose unspecified or undisclosed fees later runs against this disclosure requirement; under § 34-18-15(a)(5) a tenant may recover any fees that were not disclosed as required.
rules.tenant_explainer: Any fees on top of rent have to be spelled out in the lease, right next to the rent. A clause that lets the landlord add 'such other fees as the landlord may impose' later, without listing them, isn't how Rhode Island requires fees to be disclosed — and you can claw back fees that weren't disclosed.

citations.label: R.I. Gen. Laws § 34-18-15(a)(1)
citations.quote: If there are fees beyond the rent that apply to the rental of a unit, the lease shall disclose those fees in the same section as the rent disclosure and shall indicate that additional fees may apply.

citations.label: R.I. Gen. Laws § 34-18-15(a)(5)
citations.quote: If a landlord fails to comply with subsections (a)(1) — (a)(4) of this section, the tenant may recover any fees paid for the unit that were not disclosed as required.
